cleanIntro: The Solo is a small aluminium-framed striker pistol and it has two rules of its own: the trigger is pulled to release the striker during the strip, and the barrel leaves the slide by ROTATING 45 degrees rather than lifting straight out. ⛔ And before you reach for a solvent — the frame is anodised aluminium, so read the solvent's own label.

steps.title: Unloaded, chamber looked at
steps.action: Unload the pistol and LOOK into the chamber to confirm it is empty. This strip pulls the trigger later; the check now is what makes that safe.
steps.quote: MAKE CERTAIN THAT FIREARM IS UNLOADED BEFORE BEGINNING DISASSEMBLY.
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIP)

steps.title: Retract until the notch meets the slide stop tab
steps.action: Manually retract the slide until the slide disassembly notch lines up with the slide stop tab, then push the slide stop out from the RIGHT side of the frame.
steps.aside: Remove the slide stop from the frame by pushing it from the right side of the frame
steps.quote: Manually retract the slide until the slide disassembly notch is aligned with the slide stop tab
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIP)

steps.title: ⛔ Confirm empty AGAIN, then pull the trigger
steps.action: Kimber asks you to confirm the pistol is unloaded a second time here — and then pull the trigger to release the striker from the sear. The repeat is not padding: this is the moment the procedure requires a trigger pull, and the slide is still on the frame.
steps.aside: Move the slide assembly forward until it is removed from the frame
steps.quote: Confirm that the firearm is unloaded then, pull the
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIP)

steps.title: Invert the slide, recoil assembly forward and out
steps.action: Turn the slide over so the recoil spring assembly is visible, push the guide rod base forward toward the muzzle slightly, and lift it out from the rear.
steps.aside: Invert the slide assembly so the recoil spring assembly is visible
steps.quote: Push the recoil spring guide rod base forward (toward muzzle) slightly and lift from rear to remove the recoil spring assembly from the slide
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIP)

steps.title: ⛔ Rotate the barrel 45 degrees, then lift — strip complete
steps.action: The Solo's barrel does not lift straight out. Rotate it 45 degrees and then lift it clear of the slide. Trying to pull it out unrotated feels like something is broken; nothing is.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide by rotating 45 degrees and lifting
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIP)

steps.title: ⛔ Rod from the chamber end, and mind the ALUMINIUM frame
steps.action: Cleaning rod always in at the chamber. Wet patch, soak, dry patch, wet bore brush from the chamber end with several passes, dry patch, repeat until clean, then a light oil. ⛔ And check your solvent: the Solo's frame is anodised aluminium and not every bore cleaner is safe on it.
steps.aside: The frame of a Solo firearm is aluminum. Take special care to read all directions of cleaning solvents to ensure they are safe to use on anodized aluminum.
steps.quote: Always insert the cleaning rod from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING / LUBRICATION

steps.title: Breech face and bearing surfaces, nylon brush
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off all the bearing surfaces on slide and frame, then clean the breech face and the rest of the parts — an old toothbrush or similar nylon brush is the right tool.
steps.aside: Wipe off all dirt on all bearing surfaces on slide and frame.
steps.quote: Clean breech face and all parts (an old toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.cite: Kimber Solo Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING / LUBRICATION

steps.title: One drop per place — and NOTHING in the firing pin channel
steps.action: The Solo is designed to run on minimal lubrication, and Kimber means it: one drop per side on the slide and frame rails, one each on the trigger spring, trigger bar and sear spring, one on the barrel hood, one on the slide stop pin, one between the recoil sleeve and rod, one on the sleeve, one on the barrel exterior, and a small drop each side of the magazine catch button. ⛔ Nothing goes into the firing pin channel.
steps.aside: As a premium personal defense firearm, SOLO is designed to operate on minimal lubrication.
steps.quote: Slide and frame rails - One drop per side

deepAbsentReason: Kimber publishes nothing past the field strip for a Solo owner — the book's disassembly chapter ends with the barrel out and moves straight to cleaning. Its one explicit lubrication prohibition (nothing in the firing pin channel) is carried as a step and as a prohibition. Nothing deeper is borrowed from another source.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Barrel back into the slide, rotated 45 degrees to enter and then turned straight.
Recoil spring assembly in, guide rod base seated at the muzzle end.
Slide assembly onto the frame and run back until the disassembly notch meets the slide stop tab.
Slide stop pressed in from the left and fully seated.
Cycle the slide, then wipe off any excess lubricant.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: work the slide several times and confirm it returns fully into battery, and check the slide stop is fully seated. ⛔ A dry patch goes through the barrel before firing if it was stored oiled. Kimber's break-in note is worth honouring on this pistol — 24 rounds of 124 gr or heavier quality defence ammunition, cleaned and lubricated every 500 rounds or every session, whichever comes first.
